spans.text: The input had both a height and width of 3 and the convolution kernel had both a height and width of 2, yielding an output representation with dimension $2\times2$.

Assuming that the input shape is $n_\textrm{h}\times n_\textrm{w}$ and the convolution kernel shape is $k_\textrm{h}\times k_\textrm{w}$, the output shape will be $(n_\textrm{h}-k_\textrm{h}+1) \times (n_\textrm{w}-k_\textrm{w}+1)$: we can only shift the convolution kernel so far until it runs out of pixels to apply the convolution to.

spans.text: We will pad both sides of the width in the same way.
